items.title: FP1 washout, then Russell tops a drying FP2 ahead of Gasly
items.summary: No flying lap was set in FP1. In FP2 George Russell posted 1m 47.272s on intermediates at the very end, 0.071s ahead of Pierre Gasly and about three tenths clear of Charles Leclerc, after a short debris red flag. Hadjar was fourth and Piastri fifth.
items.why_it_matters: The order is not representative: Russell and Gasly set their times as the track was driest, and Mercedes themselves said they were not the fastest. Dry-weather tyre and long-run data is still missing, so FP3 carries unusual weight.

sources.label: Formula1.com: What the teams said - Thursday

items.title: Power-unit penalties: Antonelli, Piastri, Sainz and Stroll; Bearman to the back
items.summary: Formula1.com reports Piastri and Sainz will drop 10 places, Antonelli five (sixth ICE, after Monza), Stroll 10, while Bearman's fifth ICE, turbocharger, exhaust and MGU-K plus a new PU-ANC push him beyond 15 places, so he starts from the back. The FIA infringement notice for Piastri confirms a 10-place drop for a fifth ICE.
items.why_it_matters: Several cars will start away from their qualifying position, which changes strategy and overtaking expectations. Check the FIA documents for final confirmation of each driver.

sources.label: Formula1.com on Antonelli, Bearman and Stroll

items.title: Mercedes brings upgraded turbocharger; Antonelli only
items.summary: Antonelli is running the upgraded turbocharger and a new ICE; Russell is not on the turbocharger. Russell and the team both said the FP2 headline flattered them, with tyre consistency in the cold a worry.
items.why_it_matters: A split specification between team-mates gives an unusual read on the upgrade in FP3 and qualifying, and cold-weather graining may matter on Saturday.

items.title: Stella says further McLaren parts are planned for Las Vegas
items.summary: Stella said cooler track and ambient temperatures helped the MCL40 control tyre temperatures in Brazil, while hot-condition long-run consistency remains work in progress. He said the Interlagos upgrades will be complemented by further parts in Las Vegas as a foundation for 2027; he named no components.
items.why_it_matters: This is a team development plan, not a published FIA submission or a measured performance gain. The Las Vegas FIA listing remains inaccessible, so the component filing status is unverified.

sources.label: Formula1.com on Stella's McLaren development plan

items.title: Antonelli (Drivers') and Mercedes (Constructors') already champions
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli clinched the Drivers' title in Mexico City; Mercedes secured the Constructors' title in São Paulo.
items.why_it_matters: Both titles are decided. Las Vegas is about race wins and remaining positions, not title permutations.

sources.label: Formula1.com on the São Paulo race and Mercedes' title
